results.claim: Integral switching flows are exactly feasible points of an affine binary-parity lattice system.
results.proof_sketch: Let U be the N nonterminals. Define A_{uv}=1[s_0(u)=v]+1[s_1(u)=v] for u,v∈U and A^0_{uv}=1[s_0(u)=v]. For an integral switching flow let q_v be total outflow, ε_v=q_v mod 2, and p_v=(q_v−ε_v)/2. Integrality and 0≤x(v,s_0(v))−x(v,s_1(v))≤1 force x(v,s_0(v))=p_v+ε_v and x(v,s_1(v))=p_v. Conservation is therefore exactly M p=δ_o+Hε, where M=2I−A^T, H=(A^0)^T−I, ε∈{0,1}^N, and p∈Z_�≥0^N. Conversely, any such pair defines a nonnegative integral switching flow by those two edge formulas. The uniform walk on U is transient: from every state a sink is reached along some path of length at most N with probability at least 2^(−N), so powers of Q=A/2 tend to zero. Hence M=2(I−Q^T) is invertible and each ε has at most one rational p. With D=|det M|, integrality is equivalently the coordinatewise congruence adj(M)(δ_o+Hε)≡0 mod D, followed by nonnegativity. Terminal inflow is b_t=Σ_{s_0(u)=t}(p_u+ε_u)+Σ_{s_1(u)=t}p_u. Summing conservation gives b_0+b_1=1, so every feasible integral point has exactly one destination.

results.claim: At fixed positive-level width r, the affine system is block lower-Hessenberg and gives an exact reduction of ARRIVAL, but it retains N binary choices.
results.proof_sketch: Order U as L_1,…,L_k. If u∈L_j has an edge to v∈L_i, shortest-path distance gives j=d(u)≤d(v)+1=i+1. Thus block row i of both M and H has nonzero column blocks only among 1,…,i+1: these are r-by-r block lower-Hessenberg matrices. By the preceding bijection and the source certificate theorem, the ARRIVAL instance is YES exactly when the affine system has ε∈{0,1}^N and p∈Z_�≥0^N satisfying the displayed equation and b_1=1; every feasible point transfers back to an integral switching flow, and every integral certificate transfers into such a point. The matrices and terminal form are constructed from the graph in polynomial time. For fixed ε, exact rational solution, divisibility, nonnegativity, and the terminal condition are all testable in polynomial time. However, ε still has N=rk coordinates, and backward edges from a low level to an arbitrarily high level create entries arbitrarily far below the block diagonal. Consequently this exact reformulation does not itself give a constant-state dynamic program or a polynomial algorithm.

results.claim: Width three admits at least 2^(N/3) distinct feasible parity vectors with the same terminal signature, even when every vertex is reachable from the origin.
results.proof_sketch: For k≥1 set L_i={a_i,b_i,c_i}, put a_0=b_0=0 and c_0=1, and specify the ordered (even,odd) successors by a_i→(b_i,a_{i−1}), b_i→(a_i,b_{i−1}), and c_i→(c_{i−1},a_i). Take origin c_k. Induction shows that all three vertices indexed i have distance i: each a_i,b_i pair can leave its same-level 2-cycle only toward L_{i−1}, while c_i has its forward edge to c_{i−1}. Every vertex is graph-reachable from c_k by descending the c-rail and then using c_i→a_i→b_i. For each subset S⊆{1,…,k}, set q(c_i)=1 for every i, set q(a_i)=q(b_i)=1 for i∈S, and set all remaining outflows to zero. Since every positive q is one, only the even edge is used. The c-rail carries one unit from c_k to sink 1, while every selected pair a_i,b_i carries an isolated unit circulation. Conservation has supply one only at c_k, every switching imbalance is zero or one, and the terminal signature is always (b_0,b_1)=(0,1). The 2^k parity vectors are distinct, and N=3k. Hence enumerating all integral flows or parity points can be exponential even at width three, although this circulation family does not rule out a canonical-minimal or otherwise implicit algorithm.

results.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
results.proof_sketch: Let T be r absorbing terminals and let N be the number of nonterminals. For t∈T, let h_t(v) be the probability that the uniform random walk is absorbed at t, and put g_t(v)=h_t(v)−h_t(s_0(v)). Harmonicity gives h_t(v)−h_t(s_1(v))=−g_t(v). For switching flows x,y with the same supply φ, write d_x(v)=x(v,s_0(v))−x(v,s_1(v)). Regrouping the weighted sum Σ_(u,v)(y−x)(u,v)(h_t(u)−h_t(v)) first by vertices and then by outgoing pairs proves x^−(t)−y^−(t)=Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v). The sum is over directed edges, so antiparallel arcs remain distinct and no shared antisymmetric residual-flow variable or residual-capacity identification is assumed. Hence every terminal coordinate differs by at most Σ_v|g_t(v)|≤N/2. Total terminal inflow is fixed at Σ_vφ(v); consequently, if terminal inflows are integral, at most (⌊N/2⌋+1)^(r−1) distinct terminal-inflow vectors are possible for fixed φ. This is polynomial for fixed r. Moreover, for φ≡1 every prescribed d∈[0,1]^N is realizable: solve t_v=1+Σ_{u:s_0(u)=v}(t_u+d_u)/2+Σ_{u:s_1(u)=v}(t_u−d_u)/2. Iteration from t≡1 stays at least 1 and converges because the nonterminal transition matrix is transient. The resulting edge flows are nonnegative. Thus, for two terminals the maximum possible difference is exactly Σ_v|g(v)|, obtained by choosing d_y−d_x=sign(g).

results.claim: For fixed terminal count and fixed integral supply, all integral terminal-inflow signatures admitted by the fractional switching-flow polyhedron can be enumerated in polynomial time.
results.proof_sketch: Let P(φ) be the rational feasible region of nonnegative real switching flows with fixed supply φ. Linear programming first tests whether P(φ) is empty. For each of the first r−1 terminals, minimize and maximize its inflow over P(φ), obtaining rational endpoints α_t and β_t. The preceding duality bound gives β_t−α_t≤N/2, so each interval contains at most ⌊N/2⌋+1 integers. Enumerate their Cartesian product, set the last coordinate to Σ_vφ(v) minus the preceding coordinates, and discard negative values. For every remaining vector b, solve one LP comprising P(φ) and the equalities x^−(t)=b_t for all terminals; output b and a rational witness exactly when feasible. Every output is realizable, while every realizable integral signature lies in the enumerated ranges and has the fixed total, proving soundness and completeness. For fixed r this uses O(N^(r−1)) polynomial-size LPs. It is only a fixed-supply fractional subroutine: it neither enforces integrality of internal edge flows nor merges supply vectors created by different backward-edge flows.

results.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
results.proof_sketch: Let m_i and M_i be the minimum and maximum zero-player hitting probabilities on L_i, and W_i=M_i−m_i. A walk starting at any level at least i must hit L_{i−1} before reaching a sink. The strong Markov property therefore expresses its hitting probability as a convex combination of the values on L_{i−1}. Hence m_{i−1}≤m_i≤M_i≤M_{i−1}. Both successors of v∈L_i have level at least i−1, so |g(v)|=|h(s_0(v))−h(s_1(v))|/2≤W_{i−1}/2. For r vertices per positive level, Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_i W_{i−1}. This precisely reduces harmonic-flow stability to controlling the cumulative nested level ranges, but does not give a constant bound.

results.claim: At the one-positive-level boundary, the exact maximum gap mass is r/2; therefore the width-two stability constant fails at width three in the smallest possible depth.
results.proof_sketch: For any vertex v, harmonicity gives |g(v)|=|h(s_0(v))−h(s_1(v))|/2≤1/2. Thus a graph having only L_1 with |L_1|=r has gap mass at most r/2. Equality is attained by setting s_0(v)=0 and s_1(v)=1 for every v∈L_1: then h(v)=1/2 and |g(v)|=1/2. With common integral supply φ(v)=1, define x's outgoing pair at every vertex as (1/2,1/2) and y's as (1,0). Both have net outflow one and imbalance in [0,1], while their sink-1 inflows are r/2 and 0. The dual upper bound shows that the diameter on this graph is exactly r/2. Hence r=2 gives the sharp constant 1, whereas r=3 already gives 3/2 with one positive level, the minimum possible nonempty depth.

results.claim: For every fixed r≥3, harmonic gap mass and same-supply fractional switching-flow diameter can be Θ(N), so the universal N/2 bound is asymptotically order-tight up to an r-dependent constant.
results.proof_sketch: For k≥2 set L_i={a_i,b_i,c_i}, with a_0=0 and b_0=1. For i<k use edges a_i→(a_{i−1},a_{i+1}), b_i→(b_{i−1},b_{i+1}), and c_i→(a_{i−1},b_{i−1}). At level k use a_k→(a_{k−1},c_{k−1}), b_k→(b_{k−1},c_{k−1}), and c_k→(a_{k−1},b_{k−1}). These are exactly the positive levels because every edge decreases distance by at most one and every vertex has a forward edge. Direct substitution gives h(a_i)=i/[2(k+1)], h(b_i)=1−i/[2(k+1)], and h(c_i)=1/2. Hence Σ|g|=k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). Harmonic duality realizes this full difference with two flows having common supply φ≡1. For any fixed r>3, add r−3 centered vertices to every level with successors (a_{i−1},b_{i−1}); the original equations persist and the gap mass becomes k[4+(r−2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)]. Since N=rk, this is Θ(N) for every fixed r≥3. Thus neither a constant nor an o(N) universal gap-mass bound can extend the ladder argument.

results.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three, and two positive levels already suffice for this failure.
results.proof_sketch: Take L_1={a,b,c}, L_2={X,Y,Z}, with common edges a→(0,X), b→(0,Y), c→(0,1), and Z→(a,c). In completion A let X→(c,b) and Y→(a,b). Harmonicity gives h(c)=1/2, h(a)=h(X)/2, and h(b)=h(Y)/2, yielding h(a)=3/22>1/22=h(b). In completion B let X→(a,b) and Y→(c,a); the same equations yield h(a)=1/22<3/22=h(b). Both graphs are simple, have exactly three vertices in each positive level, and agree on the sinks and every outgoing edge from L_1. Thus no width-three rule using only the preceding order and the current vertices' outgoing edges can determine the order. With only one positive level there is no unseen higher-level completion, so depth two is the first possible boundary for this particular nonlocality obstruction.

results.claim: These obstructions delimit the width-two proof strategy but do not settle fixed-width ARRIVAL.
results.proof_sketch: The LP enumeration starts only after the complete supply vector is fixed, whereas backward edges from processed levels can create different supplies at many future vertices. Internal edge integrality is also not enforced, and equality of terminal signatures alone does not justify merging different future injections. The linear-diameter and local-order counterexamples refute two ladder-style mechanisms, but they provide neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor a hardness classification. Consequently the requested target remains unresolved even for r=3.

final_writeup:
Here “width r” necessarily means each positive level L_i, i≥1, since L_0 consists of the two sinks.

The target remains unresolved, but there is an exact structural reformulation. Let U be the N nonterminals. For an integral switching flow, write q_v for the total outflow of v, ε_v=q_v mod 2, and p_v=(q_v−ε_v)/2. The switching rule forces the even- and odd-edge flows to be p_v+ε_v and p_v. If A records both internal successors and A^0 records the even internal successor, conservation becomes

(2I−A^T)p = δ_o + ((A^0)^T−I)ε,   ε∈{0,1}^N,   p∈Z_�≥0^N.

Conversely, every feasible pair (ε,p) produces an integral switching flow. The internal uniform-walk matrix A/2 is transient, so M=2I−A^T is invertible. Hence every ε determines at most one rational p. Equivalently, with D=|det M|, integrality is the coordinatewise divisibility condition adj(M)(δ_o+((A^0)^T−I)ε)≡0 mod D, followed by nonnegativity. Terminal inflows are explicit affine forms in p and ε, and their sum is one. By the switching-flow certificate theorem, the instance is YES exactly when this system has a feasible point whose sink-1 inflow is one.

Ordering variables by L_1,…,L_k exposes the promised width structure. An edge from L_j to L_i satisfies j≤i+1, so M and ((A^0)^T−I) are r-by-r block lower-Hessenberg matrices. Construction of the system and checking a fixed ε are polynomial-time operations. However, ε still has N=rk binary coordinates, and long backward edges create entries arbitrarily far below the block diagonal. The reformulation therefore isolates the discrete obstacle without solving it.

Indeed, feasible parity vectors cannot simply be listed. For width three, let L_i={a_i,b_i,c_i}, set a_0=b_0=0 and c_0=1, and give the vertices ordered successors a_i→(b_i,a_{i−1}), b_i→(a_i,b_{i−1}), and c_i→(c_{i−1},a_i), with origin c_k. These are exactly the positive levels, and every vertex is graph-reachable from the origin. For every subset S of the k levels, send one unit along each even c-rail edge and, for i∈S, one unit around the even 2-cycle a_i↔b_i. This yields 2^k=2^(N/3) distinct integral switching flows and parity vectors, all with terminal signature (0,1). Thus complete parity-point enumeration is exponential even at width three. These optional circulations do not exclude a canonical-minimal or implicit polynomial algorithm.

Separately, the retained harmonic duality yields a constructive fixed-supply subroutine. For q absorbing boundary terminals, let h_t be the absorption probability at terminal t and let g_t(v)=h_t(v)−h_t(s_0(v)). For switching flows x,y with the same supply φ, directed summation by parts gives

x^−(t)−y^−(t)=Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v),

where d_x(v)=x(v,s_0(v))−x(v,s_1(v))∈[0,1]. Thus each terminal-inflow coordinate has diameter at most Σ_v|g_t(v)|≤N/2, while total terminal inflow is the fixed integer Σφ.

After φ is fixed, optimize each of the first q−1 terminal coordinates over the rational switching-flow polyhedron. Each resulting interval contains at most ⌊N/2⌋+1 integers. Enumerate their Cartesian product, derive the last coordinate from Σφ, and run an equality-constrained LP for every candidate. For fixed q, O(N^(q−1)) LPs list exactly all integral terminal signatures admitted by fractional flows. This still neither enforces internal integrality nor merges supply vectors generated by different backward-edge flows.

A general level estimate explains another limitation. If [m_i,M_i] is the range of a two-terminal hitting probability on L_i, first hitting of L_{i−1} gives nested ranges [m_i,M_i]⊆[m_{i−1},M_{i−1}]. Hence

Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_i(M_{i−1}−m_{i−1}).

This can be linear in the depth. With only L_1, the exact maximum is already r/2: assigning every vertex even edge to 0 and odd edge to 1 attains it. Thus the width-two constant one fails at width three with diameter 3/2. In the three-rail family the gap mass is k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k), and padding gives k[4+(r−2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)]=Θ(N) for every fixed r≥3. No constant or sublinear gap-mass bound can extend the ladder proof in general.

The width-two local-order mechanism also fails: two width-three graphs with identical sinks and identical outgoing edges from L_1 can have (h(a),h(b))=(3/22,1/22) and (1/22,3/22), depending on their L_2 completion.

Accordingly, the reformulation and obstruction families provide no polynomial-time algorithm or contrary complexity classification. Varying future supplies, selection of a useful integral parity point, and a sound way to ignore or normalize circulations remain unresolved even for r=3. The claimed resolution is PARTIAL, not FULL.
